summary: Phased billing adjustment created zero-dollar line and removed provisional credits mid-cycle
description:
Issue summary:
BrightCart Labs reported that their mid-cycle invoice (billing cycle 2026-03) shows a zero-dollar line item labeled "phased billing adjustment" and several provisional credits were removed by the system, causing overage alerts and a net unexpected increase in the balance. The customer is on Dedicated capacity and had a short burst/rollback window on 2026-03-10.

Impact:
- Customer invoiced balance appears higher than expected; automated overage alerts triggered.
- Billing UI shows a zero-dollar adjustment line (no clear explanation).
- Customer requests explanation and a correction or provisional credit while we investigate.

Environment:
- Production (prod-us-east)
- Org: BrightCart Labs (dedicated pool: BRIGHT-POOL-1)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Run reconciliation for hourly postbacks for 2026-03-10 02:00–04:00 UTC for BRIGHT-POOL-1.
2. Billing-engine created phased adjustments for reserved-hour prorates and applied tax rounding.
3. One aggregated adjustment resulted in a zero-dollar line (rounded to 0.00) and removed an earlier provisional credit line from 2026-03-09.
4. Invoicing UI shows |Adjustment: phased billing adjustment| amount: $0.00 and a missing provisional-credit line.

Logs / evidence (relevant extracts):
- billing-engine job id: bill-reconcile-20260310-02 (trace id: 6f4a9f)
- postback aggregation snapshot: /s3/billing/brightcart/2026-03-10/agg-02.json (customer provided)
- invoice number: INV-2026-03-BR-4512 (screenshot attached by customer)
- alert: usage-overage-email-2026-03-12 (timestamped 2026-03-12T08:10:00Z)

Initial hypothesis:
- Hourly postback re-aggregation after a reserved-capacity rollback duplicated a prorate adjustment window and a subsequent tax-rounding pass zeroed the net amount, which suppressed the earlier provisional credit in the UI.
- Edge-case in phased_adjustment pipeline: when positive provisional credits and negative prorates net to < $0.005, rounding logic collapsed the line to $0.00 and a downstream dedup step removed the provisional credit reference.

Customer request:
- Explanation of what happened and a corrected invoice or provisional credit until the next statement.
- Confirmation that this will not count as an actual overage charge while under investigation.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Ava Martinez (Support): Thanks for the report — I see the INV-2026-03-BR-4512 you attached. Marking this P1 and escalating to Billing/Payments. Can you confirm the exact time window of the dedicated burst?

2026-03-13 09:25 - John Park (BrightCart Labs): The burst started at 2026-03-10T02:10Z and we rolled back at 2026-03-10T03:05Z. We saw an alert the next day and the invoice line appeared after the automated reconciliation. We'd like provisional credit until fixed.

2026-03-13 10:03 - Rahul Menon (Billing Engineer): Assigned. Pulling postback logs and reconciliation trace (bill-reconcile-20260310-02). Preliminary check shows a double-prorate window overlapping with a tax-rounder pass. Holding off on charging customer pending investigation; applying internal hold flag to org (billing_hold:true).

2026-03-13 13:48 - Mei Chen (Payments): Found that phased_adjustment step 2 collapsed a -0.0023 net adjustment to 0.00 after tax rounding. The provisional credit line reference id (prov-20260309-bright-11) was removed by dedup because it matched the adjustment footprint. Need to decide: re-run aggregation with high-precision rounding or apply manual correction.
investigation_notes: Billing-engine trace details: recon job processed three events for BRIGHT-POOL-1 in the 02:00-04:00 window. Sequence: (1) reserved-prorate apply, (2) provisional-credit revert, (3) tax-rounder normalize. The dedup/filter stage uses a hash of (org, window, ledger_tag). When provisional_credit and prorate net to less than $0.005, tax-rounder normalized to 0.00 and filter considered it duplicate with the earlier provisional id and removed display of the provisional line. Reproducer: unit test added using sample payloads from S3 path. Root cause candidate: insufficient decimal precision in phased_adjustment pipeline + dedup heuristics. Priority fix: change rounding to banker's rounding at 4 decimal places and update dedup to consider original provisional id when netting near-zero adjustments.
resolution_notes: Action taken 2026-03-14: Applied manual provisional credit for BrightCart Labs ($1,234.56) to offset the discrepancy while we reprocess the reconciliation. Re-ran billing-engine reconcile for 2026-03-10 (job id reproc-20260314-08) with updated rounding flags — provisional-credit lines retained and zero-dollar collapsed lines are now expanded to show +/- $0.00 with explanation note. Final invoice adjusted and credit memo CM-2026-03-BR-78 issued. Customer notified and confirmed acceptance. Follow-up ticket created to deploy rounding/dedup fix in next billing release.
next_steps: Code: merge PR to update phased_adjustment rounding and dedup heuristics (owner: Mei Chen).
Release: include change in billing-engine 2026-03-20 patch release; smoke test with BRIGHT-POOL-1 sample.
Communicate: send final resolution email + credit memo to BrightCart Labs (owner: Ava Martinez).
Postmortem: document root cause and add runbook step to hold orgs while mid-cycle reprocessing occurs (owner: Rahul Menon).
